posts.title: Two guitars, one garden house (Casula + Loculus)
posts.igCaption:
My house came with a garden house. It became my workshop.

The wood of its shelves became the top of Sixto Loculus. The wood I still had left from it became the herringbone top of Sixto Casula.

Two guitars. One garden house. Loculus: Latin for a small compartment. Casula: a little house.

What would you build from the place you live in?

posts.title: Ebony, 12" radius (Horreum)
posts.igCaption:
An ebony fretboard for Horreum. 🪵

Rough-cut to a 12" radius with my router and radius jig. That curve is what your fingers feel on every chord. Sanding it true comes next.

Ever wondered why some necks just feel right? Ask me anything below.

posts.title: Every neck starts as a plank (Short, v2)
posts.note: v2: opent met de ruwe neck blank van Rupes, trager, met de ebben toets van Horreum. Instagram is al gepost; dit is voor de YouTube Short.
posts.igCaption:
Every neck starts as a plank. 🪵

A channel for the truss rod, which works against the pull of the strings. Then the fretboard. Then the frets. Then, finally, someone plays it.

Three guitars in this one: Horreum on the bench now, the frets of Solum, and the finished neck of Rupes.

#SixtoCustomGuitars #HandmadeGuitar #ReclaimedWood #OneOfOne #Luthier #GuitarBuilding #GuitarNeck #MadeByHand #CraftedNotManufactured #BelgianMade
posts.igCaptionLong:
Every neck starts as a plank.

You never see most of the work that goes into a neck. First a channel is routed for the truss rod: the steel rod inside that works against the pull of the strings, so the neck stays the way it should.

Then the fretboard goes on. Then the frets. And only then does it become something you can play.

In this reel, three guitars: Horreum, on the bench right now; the frets of Solum; and the finished neck of Rupes.

posts.ytDescription:
Most of the work in a neck stays invisible. A truss rod inside, the steel rod that works against the pull of the strings. Then the fretboard: ebony, rough-cut to a 12" radius with my radius jig. Then the frets, and only then can it be played.

Three handmade guitars in one Short: Rupes (the raw neck blank, and the finished guitar), Horreum (truss rod and ebony fretboard, on the bench now) and Solum (frets). Built by hand in Belgium from reclaimed wood.

posts.title: Sixto Horreum: barn wood (reel + Short)
posts.note: Reel 28 s. Post op Instagram en als YouTube Short.
posts.igCaption:
These boards were part of a barn for over a hundred years. The hinges and nails came out of them, the rings tell the rest. 🪵

Old-growth pine: the trees were already old long before the barn was built. Now it's becoming a semi-hollow called Horreum, Latin for barn.

From barn boards to body blank to neck. Fretboard is next. Follow along.

#handmadeguitar #luthier #reclaimedwood #oldgrowth #barnwood #semihollow #customguitar #guitarbuild #sixtocustomguitars #oneofone #woodwithastory #belgianmade
posts.igCaptionLong:
New build on the bench, and this one comes with some serious history.

These boards spent over a hundred years as part of a barn. The old hinges and nails came out of them before anything else happened. The wood is old-growth pine, so the trees were growing long before anyone thought of building that barn. You can see it in the end grain: tight rings, slow growth, the kind of wood you can't just order.

Every Sixto gets a name from the wood's previous life. This one is Horreum: Latin for barn.

The body is glued up and will become a semi-hollow, the neck has its truss rod, and the fretboard is next. And yes, sighting down a neck with one eye closed is a perfectly legitimate measuring technique.

Follow along to see a barn turn into a guitar.
